cells.tense: You're in a clearing, and your mind is quiet enough to know what still belongs here and what doesn't.
cells.ask: Pass one thing you know on to someone in a way that leaves them free to change it — see what comes back.
cells.core:
A kitchen being cleared after a long meal is the picture that fits: you know what to keep, you know what to carry out, and you do it because it's done, not because you're afraid of what's left. There's an ending underway and you're awake inside it. Not rushing it and not clinging to what's already leaving — you can sort what's finished from what's just gone quiet, and you're letting each go at its own pace.

What you know about how this ends doesn't stay with you. You hand it over intact enough to be useful and loose enough that whoever receives it can make it theirs. They'll change it. That's the point — it stays alive past the moment it stops being yours.
cells.sheetLine: You can sort what's finished from what's just resting, and you're letting each go on its own terms.
cells.verb: Letting the mind lie still on purpose until it settles into its own balance
cells.place: Where what was has to fully end before what comes next can begin

cells.tense: You're already living past the ending, rehearsing what comes after it, while the thing itself is still here.
cells.ask: Pick one direction and hold it on what you actually feel about this, not on what you've decided you'll feel once it's over.
cells.core:
You're bracing for a future you can't write yet, and the bracing is doing the deciding. The ending hasn't finished and you've already moved into the next room — planning it, defending it, working out who you'll be on the other side. There's no quiet in that, no rest, just momentum pointed at a door that isn't open.

A kitchen being cleared at the end of a long day is what this looks like with the balance on: you carry things out because they're over, and you move at the speed of what actually happened. The clearing keeps pace with the ending. You feel your way through it instead of outrunning it.
cells.sheetLine: You've already left an ending you're still standing in.
cells.verb: Letting the mind lie still on purpose until it settles into its own balance
cells.place: Where what was has to fully end before what comes next can begin

cells.tense: You stopped at the threshold a while back, and you're still standing there, treating it like it's ahead of you.
cells.ask: Let one feeling about someone you'd want near you actually arrive — no plan for what you'll do with it — and see what it pulls.
cells.core:
The ending is here and you're not in it. You've been sitting at the edge of something that already changed, holding still, and the stillness has stopped being rest and become a place to not move from. Your mind isn't quiet — it's quiet because nothing's being let through.

Picture a room getting lighter as things get put away. You notice what's gone, you feel the space open up, and you do it with someone there, even briefly. That lightness needs you in the room and feeling something. There's connection already waiting on the other side of the clearing, and it starts with you letting a feeling arrive.
cells.sheetLine: You're standing at a threshold that already passed you.
cells.verb: Letting the mind lie still on purpose until it settles into its own balance
cells.place: Where what was has to fully end before what comes next can begin

cells.tense: You're already deciding what stays and what goes — you just haven't noticed that's what you're doing.
cells.ask: Say out loud that one ending is yours to make — to one person, in plain words — and let it be true because you said it.
cells.core:
Things are leaving your life right now because of choices you're already making, and you're describing those choices like they happened to you. The clearing is happening. The hand doing the clearing is yours, and you keep talking like it's no one's.

A table people gather at runs on this being said out loud — who's at it, what gets carried forward, what won't. Some have been there a long while, some just sat down, and the table stays alive because someone keeps choosing, openly, what belongs on it. That someone is you. The choosing works better when it's spoken than when it's assumed.
cells.sheetLine: You're already doing the clearing. You just haven't claimed it.
